title: Mini Social Feed
statement:
Build the core of a tiny social network: users post short messages, follow each other, and read a home feed.

  • Twitter() creates an empty network. Users are identified by ids and need no sign-up; a user who has done nothing simply has nothing to show.
  • postTweet(userId, tweetId): the user posts a message with id tweetId. Message ids are unique, and every call happens later than the one before it. The ids themselves are not in time order.
  • getNewsFeed(userId) returns the ids of the 10 most recent messages posted by the user or by anyone the user currently follows, newest first. If there are fewer than 10, return all of them; with none, return [].
  • follow(followerId, followeeId): the follower starts following the followee. Following someone you already follow changes nothing.
  • unfollow(followerId, followeeId): the follower stops following the followee, and the followee's messages, old ones included, leave the feed. Unfollowing someone you do not follow changes nothing.

Users always see their own messages. Following or unfollowing yourself does nothing: your own messages stay in your feed either way.

Tests are written as a list of operations and their arguments; the first operation creates the network. The expected output has one entry per operation (null where nothing is returned).

examples.why: The feed is ordered by posting time, not by id: 7 was posted after 40. Following user 2 also brings in 2's older message, and unfollowing removes it again.
Unfollowing yourself does nothing, so 21 stays. User 9 has never posted or followed anyone, so the feed is empty.

hints: Ids are not in time order, so you need your own clock. What should you store for each post?
Store each user's posts in their own list, oldest first, tagged with a global counter. A feed then needs the 10 newest items across several lists that are each already sorted by time.
That is a k-way merge. Put the newest post of each relevant user into a max-heap keyed on time. Pop 10 times; after each pop, push the next older post from the same user.

explain.intuition:
Give every post a timestamp from a global counter, because the ids carry no order. Each user's posts then form a list that is already sorted by time, simply because you append. A feed is the newest 10 posts across the lists of the user and everyone they follow: a k-way merge of sorted lists, the same idea as merging several sorted lists into one, except you stop after 10 items.

For the merge, put the newest post of each relevant user into a max-heap keyed on time. The top is the newest post overall. Pop it, and push that same user's next older post, which is now that user's best candidate. After 10 pops you are done, no matter how many posts exist. This is how a real home timeline is built "on read" from per-author streams. Follows are a map from user to a set, so follow and unfollow are O(1). The feed is always computed from the current follows, which makes unfollow hide old posts automatically.
steps: Keep a counter time, a map posts from user to a list of [time, tweetId], and a map follows from user to a set of followees.
postTweet: append [time++, tweetId] to the user's list.
follow and unfollow: add to or remove from the set, ignoring a user's own id.
getNewsFeed(u): for u and every followee with posts, push [time of last post, user, index] into a max-heap.
Pop up to 10 times. Each pop adds its tweet id to the feed; if that user has an older post at index − 1, push it.
pitfalls: Sorting by tweet id instead of by posting time. Example 1 posts 40 before 7, so an id sort gets the feed wrong.
Adding a user to their own follow set, or listing them both as "self" and as a followee. Their posts then show up twice in the feed.
Collecting every post of every followee and sorting them all on each read. It is correct, but each read costs the full history instead of about 10 heap steps.

complexity.time: O(1) post, follow and unfollow; O(f + 10 log f) per feed, f = number of followees

solutions.title: One global timeline, scanned backwards
solutions.idea: Keep every post in one list in posting order. A feed walks from the newest post back and keeps the ones by the user or a followee, until it has 10.
solutions.time: O(1) post, O(total posts) per feed in the worst case

solutions.title: Per-user timelines + heap merge
solutions.idea: Each user's posts are a list sorted by time. A feed merges the lists of the user and their followees with a max-heap and stops after 10 posts.
solutions.time: O(f + 10 log f) per feed, O(1) otherwise

followups: A celebrity has ten million followers. Would you build feeds on read like this, or push each new post into followers' feeds on write? What are the trade-offs?
Add getNewsFeed(userId, page) that returns the next 10 older posts. What state would you keep between calls?
